Since \(2n+1 \mid n^2+1\), reduce modulo \(2n+1\). We have
\[
2n \equiv -1 \pmod{2n+1}.
\]
Squaring gives
\[
4n^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{2n+1}.
\]
From \(n^2+1 \equiv 0\), multiply by \(4\):
\[
4n^2+4 \equiv 0 \pmod{2n+1}.
\]
Thus
\[
1+4 \equiv 5 \equiv 0 \pmod{2n+1}.
\]
So \(2n+1 \mid 5\). Since \(2n+1 \ge 3\), we get
\[
2n+1=5 \implies n=2.
\]
Check: \(2^4+2^2=20\), divisible by \(5\).

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
